Do not edit it: change the schema and run `node tools/guide/generate-reference.cjs --write`. The schemas are the authority and [the CLI contract](../../contracts/cli-v1.md) says what each command promises; this page is for finding a member quickly. Every command prints one of these documents with `--json`, wrapped in the envelope of [operation-response.schema.json](#operation-responseschemajson).

## Failure codes

The `error.code` of a failed result is one of these (the schema's own list). What each one means and what to do is in [troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md).

- `INTERNAL`
- `INVALID_ARGUMENT`
- `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA`
- `MISSING_CAPABILITY`
- `ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE`
- `COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`
- `INVALID_SOURCE`
- `BUSY`
- `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`
- `RESOURCE_LIMIT`
- `CANCELLED`
- `STORAGE_IO`
- `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`
- `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`
- `DOWNLOAD_FAILED`

## Schemas

### audio-data.schema.json

**VSift audio data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/audio-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial audio result (P09, ADR 0019): one WAV clip of at most 30 s of the session's audio (16 kHz mono signed 16-bit, decision D5). request is the requested half-open range; a range that runs past the end of the source is clipped to it and range_clipped is true. The single selection has role requested, requested_us the requested start, actual_us the first decoded sample's time and delta_us their difference. items holds the audio_evidence record, files delivers the clip as the absolute path of the committed session artifact, valid while the session exists (decision D2). With reused true the record was committed by an identical earlier request and returned without running a provider or writing anything. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `operation` | constant "audio" | yes |  |
| `request` | object | yes |  |
| `request.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `request.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical request, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. An identical later request with a known fingerprint is answered from the complete record with this key.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `reused` | boolean | yes | true when the record was committed by an earlier identical request and returned without running a provider or writing anything; every file was verified again. |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter, reviewed policy, host isolation and verifying authority), or null when it could not be computed; then the evidence_id also digests the image and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_check` | "identity" \| "full_hash" | yes | How the call that committed the record checked the session's source copy (decision D1): identity (its on-disk identity matched the one recorded after an earlier full hash) or full_hash. |
| `selections` | array of object | yes | Which item each requested time resolved to. requested_us is the time the role refers to: the requested time (requested, frame_get), the anchor frame's time (before and after), a burst target's time (target) or the parent frame's time (requested, crop). delta_us is actual_us - requested_us.; exactly 1 items |
| `selections[].role` | constant "requested" | no |  |
| `range_clipped` | boolean | yes | true when the requested range ran past the end of the source and the clip covers only its part before the end. |
| `items` | array of object, see [audio-evidence.schema.json](#audio-evidenceschemajson) | yes | exactly 1 items |
| `files` | array of object | yes | One delivered file per item, in item order: the absolute path of the committed session artifact (decision D2). It is valid while the session exists (until it is closed, expires or is cleaned) and must not be written to; retain the session to keep the evidence.; exactly 1 items |
| `files[].media_type` | constant "audio/wav" | no |  |
| `partial_reason` | "frame_budget" \| "pixel_budget" \| "byte_budget" \| "session_evidence_budget" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "cancelled" or null | yes | Why the call returned fewer items than its request named, or null for a complete result. The items returned are committed evidence. Only complete records are reused. |

### audio-evidence.schema.json

**VSift audio evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/audio-evidence.schema.json))

One published audio_evidence record (P09, ADR 0019): a WAV clip of the session's audio, extracted by audio. Its evidence_id digests only what fixes its samples (session, source, audio stream, adapter profile, provider fingerprint and the clipped range), so every request that resolves to the same range names the same record. range is the half-open range the clip was decoded for (the request clipped to the source); actual_start_us is the normalized time of the first decoded sample, which may lie after range.start_us (for example AAC priming or a stream that starts late). The samples are the delivered file named in the result's files, never embedded. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock_time` | any or any | no | The clip's real-world clock times (time anchoring, 0.3.0): start and end of its planned range, and at, its first decoded sample (actual_start_us); absent when the session has no time anchor. See time-anchor.schema.json. |
| `clock_time.source` | "operator" \| "quicktime_creationdate" \| "container_creation_time" | yes |  |
| `clock_time.confidence` | "exact" \| "high" \| "medium" | yes |  |
| `clock_time.at` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.at.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.at.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.at.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `clock_time.start` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.start.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.start.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.start.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `clock_time.end` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.end.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.end.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |

### bundle-evidence-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-evidence-record.schema.json))

The content of a session or retained bundle artifact whose kind is evidence_record (P09, ADR 0019): the lineage of one evidence call (frame get, frame neighbours, frame burst, crop or audio), stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version and format names the record. It holds the call's request key and canonical parameters, which item each requested time resolved to with requested and actual time and their signed delta, the items (stream, exact timestamp and time base, crop region or clipped audio range, the digest and size of the frame_png or audio_wav artifact that holds the pixels or samples, the provider fingerprint and how the call checked the source copy) and why the call stopped short, if it did. It never holds an operation identifier, a path or media bytes. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. A session holds at most 384 evidence artifacts (images, clips and records together) within 512 artifacts and a record is at most 256 KiB. bundle validate decodes every record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected), re-derives the request key and every item identity, checks that each item's file is in the bundle with the item's kind, size and digest, that an image's PNG header states the item's dimensions and a clip's WAV header 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit PCM, that every crop parent and neighbours anchor is an item of the bundle, and that items with one identity agree on everything but their source check. This schema describes its shape.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.evidence_record" | yes |  |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical parameters, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. A later call with the same key and a known fingerprint is answered from a complete record without running a provider.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter and policy), or null when it could not be computed; then the item identity also digests the media and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `request` | object or object or object or object or object | yes | The canonical request, named by its operation. |
| `request.frame_get` | object | yes |  |

### bundle-screen-text-index-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle screen-text index record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-screen-text-index-record.schema.json))

The content of a session or retained bundle artifact whose kind is screen_text_index_record (0.3.0, ADR 0030): one immutable revision of the session's on-screen text index, stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version and format names the record. Each ocr call that attempts a frame commits one; a revision holds every frame of the revision before it read by the same engine build, so only the newest is read. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. The record holds no pixels, only what was read and where. A session holds at most 64 such records of at most 48 MiB. Releases before 0.3.0 do not know the kind and refuse a session or bundle that holds one. bundle validate decodes every record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected) and checks what a record could claim without being true: frames in ascending pts order, each with a target, regions inside their frame, the bounds below, and every index and line identity derived again from the session, source, stream, profile, engine build, frame and line ordinal. This schema describes its shape.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.screen_text_index_record" | yes |  |
| `index_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sti_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `revision` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `stream_index` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `profile` | "ppocrv5-latin-v1" | yes |  |
| `engine` | object | yes |  |
| `engine.runner_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `engine.runner_version` | string | yes | 1 to 64 characters; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` |
| `engine.runtime_version` | string | yes | 1 to 64 characters; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` |
| `engine.detector_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `engine.recognizer_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `period_us` | integer | yes | The period of the latest call's plan.; 1000000 to 600000000 |
| `frames` | array of object | yes | Frames attempted, in strictly ascending pts order.; at most 4096 items |
| `frames[].pts` | integer | yes |  |
| `frames[].time_base` | array of integer | yes | [numerator, denominator] of the stream's time base.; exactly 2 items; each: 1 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].time_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `frames[].width` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].height` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].targets` | array of object | yes | at least 1 items |
| `frames[].targets[].time_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `frames[].targets[].candidate_id` | string | no | pattern `^vcd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |

| `frames[].lines[].id` | string | yes | pattern `^stl_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `frames[].lines[].x` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].lines[].y` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].lines[].width` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].lines[].height` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `frames[].lines[].text` | string | yes | 1 to 512 characters |
| `frames[].lines[].confidence_bp` | integer | yes | The engine's uncalibrated score in basis points.; 0 to 10000 |
| `unresolved` | array of object | yes | Planned targets that resolved to no decodable frame.; at most 4096 items |
| `unresolved[].time_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `unresolved[].candidate_id` | string | no | pattern `^vcd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |

### bundle-transcript-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle transcript record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-transcript-record.schema.json))

The content of a retained bundle artifact whose bundle.json kind is transcript_record: one immutable transcript revision with all of its segments, stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version (1 for an imported revision, 2 for a local-ASR revision) and format names the record. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. text is the stored segment text with recognised markup removed (lines joined with \n; no other control character). Text is untrusted input: sanitize it before display. bundle validate decodes every transcript record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected) and re-checks every segment against the rule that produced it; this schema describes its shape.

### bundle-visual-index-record.schema.json

**VSift retained bundle visual-index record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/bundle-visual-index-record.schema.json))

The content of a session or retained bundle artifact whose kind is visual_index_record (P08): one immutable revision of the session's visual-candidate index, stored as compact UTF-8 JSON and named artifact-<sha256>.json. This is a storage record, not an operation response: schema_version is the integer record version and format names the record. A revision holds every window of the revision before it unchanged, so only the newest is read; windows that are absent have not been analysed. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. The record holds no pixels or sample data, only candidates. A session holds at most 64 such records of at most 8 MiB. bundle validate decodes every record strictly (unknown fields, values and newer versions are rejected) and re-derives what a record could claim without being true: each window's range from its ordinal and duration_us, each candidate's span start from its representative time and its end from the next candidate or the window end, sample counts, every change against the r0-visual-v1 policy, that every 10 s cell holds a candidate or is listed in frameless_cells, and every candidate and revision identity from the session, source, stream, profile, window and time. This schema describes its shape.

| `schema_version` | constant 1 | yes |  |
| `format` | constant "vsift.visual_index_record" | yes |  |
| `index_id` | string | yes | pattern `^vix_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `revision` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `stream_index` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `displayed_dimensions` | object | yes |  |

### candidates-brief-data.schema.json

**VSift candidates data, brief view v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/candidates-brief-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial candidates result asked for with --view brief (0.2.1): candidates-data.schema.json with each item reduced to visual-candidate-brief.schema.json, a view member that is always brief and item_constants, which holds once what the full view repeats on every candidate of the index. The requested range, the index, the coverage with every typed gap and the cursor are the full page's own: what was and was not analysed is never left out. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial, exactly when coverage.gaps is not empty. The view is refused with --events jsonl. Pass next_cursor back with the same session and range to continue; it never analyses anything, and the view is not part of what a cursor binds, so it continues in either view.

| `range` | object | yes |  |
| `range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `index` | object | yes | The committed visual-index revision the page was read from. Each call that analyses anything commits a new revision holding every window of the one before it unchanged, so candidate identities never change. |

| `index.number` | integer | yes | 1 to 64 |
| `index.profile` | constant "r0-visual-v1" | yes |  |
| `index.duration_us` | integer | yes | The video's probed duration; windows and coverage are clipped to it.; at least 1 |

| `index.sample_interval_us` | constant 500000 | yes | Decoded frames are sampled at least this far apart (2 Hz). |

| `item_constants.source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `item_constants.source_segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `item_constants.stream_index` | integer | yes | 0 to 4294967295 |
| `item_constants.displayed_dimensions` | object | yes |  |
| `item_constants.displayed_dimensions.width` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `item_constants.displayed_dimensions.height` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `item_constants.analysis` | object | yes |  |

| `item_constants.analysis.width` | constant 128 | yes |  |
| `item_constants.analysis.height` | constant 72 | yes |  |
| `coverage` | object | yes |  |
| `coverage.searched_range` | object | yes | The requested range clipped to the video. |
| `coverage.searched_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.searched_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `coverage.analyzed` | array of object | yes | Parts of searched_range that analysed windows cover, merged and in start order. no_decoded_frame and candidate_budget_exhausted gaps lie inside them.; at most 100 items |
| `coverage.analyzed[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.analyzed[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `coverage.gaps` | array of object | yes | Every typed gap of searched_range in start order; touching gaps of one reason are merged, except budget gaps, which stay per window.; at most 100 items |
| `coverage.gaps[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.gaps[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |

### evidence-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL evidence record event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/evidence-event.schema.json))

One evidence record in an --events jsonl stream. Evidence events precede the single terminal event (terminal-event.schema.json) that ends the stream; sequence numbers start at 0 and are contiguous across every event of the stream. record_type names the schema of record. key is the record's upsert key: evidence records are immutable, so the same (record_type, key) always carries the same record and a consumer may upsert by it idempotently.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant "1" | yes |  |
| `event` | constant "evidence" | yes |  |
| `sequence` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `command` | string | yes | at most 64 characters; pattern `^[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*(?:[.][a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*)?$` |
| `operation_id` | string or null | yes | pattern `^op_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `record_type` | "transcript_segment" \| "visual_candidate" \| "frame_evidence" \| "audio_evidence" | yes |  |
| `key` | string | yes | at most 128 characters; pattern `^[a-z]+_[a-z0-9_]+$` |
| `record` | object | yes |  |

This schema also holds 4 conditional rules (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/evidence-event.schema.json) for them.

### frame-data.schema.json

**VSift frame and crop data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/frame-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial frame.get, frame.neighbours, frame.burst or crop result (P09, ADR 0019). operation names the call and fixes the shape of request, neighbours and burst. The result presents the lineage record the call committed, or, with reused true, the complete record an identical earlier request committed (no provider ran and nothing was written). selections say which item each requested time resolved to, with requested and actual time and their signed delta; items are the distinct frame_evidence records in the record's order; files deliver each item's image as the absolute path of the committed session artifact, valid while the session exists and never to be written to (decision D2). A result whose call stopped on a budget, the deadline or a cancellation after extracting something has partial_reason set and envelope status partial. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `operation` | "frame_get" \| "frame_neighbours" \| "frame_burst" \| "crop" | yes |  |
| `request` | object | yes |  |
| `request_key` | string | yes | Digest of the session, source, stream selector, operation, canonical request, adapter profile and provider fingerprint. An identical later request with a known fingerprint is answered from the complete record with this key.; pattern `^opk_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `reused` | boolean | yes | true when the record was committed by an earlier identical request and returned without running a provider or writing anything; every file was verified again. |
| `profile` | constant "p09-r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `tool_fingerprint` | string or null | yes | The media provider's fingerprint (executables' identity, adapter, reviewed policy, host isolation and verifying authority), or null when it could not be computed; then the evidence_id also digests the image and nothing is reused.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_check` | "identity" \| "full_hash" | yes | How the call that committed the record checked the session's source copy (decision D1): identity (its on-disk identity matched the one recorded after an earlier full hash) or full_hash. |
| `selections` | array of object | yes | Which item each requested time resolved to. requested_us is the time the role refers to: the requested time (requested, frame_get), the anchor frame's time (before and after), a burst target's time (target) or the parent frame's time (requested, crop). delta_us is actual_us - requested_us.; 1 to 100 items |
| `selections[].role` | "requested" \| "before" \| "after" \| "target" | yes |  |
| `selections[].evidence_id` | string | yes | pattern `^evd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `selections[].requested_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `selections[].actual_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `selections[].delta_us` | integer | yes |  |
| `neighbours` | object or null | yes | For frame_neighbours, why each side stopped short; null for every other operation. |
| `neighbours.before_stop` | "start_of_stream" \| "end_of_stream" \| "search_window" or null | yes | Why a side holds fewer frames than asked: start_of_stream, end_of_stream, or search_window (the frames searched ended; more may exist). null when the side is full. |
| `neighbours.after_stop` | "start_of_stream" \| "end_of_stream" \| "search_window" or null | yes | Why a side holds fewer frames than asked: start_of_stream, end_of_stream, or search_window (the frames searched ended; more may exist). null when the side is full. |
| `burst` | object or null | yes | For frame_burst, the plan: the range the even targets were spread over (the requested range, or its part before the end of the video with extent clipped_at_end_of_stream), the number of targets and the number of distinct frames they named; null for every other operation. |
| `burst.planned` | object | yes |  |
| `burst.planned.start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `burst.planned.end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `burst.extent` | "requested" \| "clipped_at_end_of_stream" | yes |  |
| `burst.targets` | integer | yes | 1 to 100 |
| `burst.distinct` | integer | yes | 0 to 100 |
| `items` | array of object, see [frame-evidence.schema.json](#frame-evidenceschemajson) | yes | The distinct items, in the record's order; each is a frame_evidence record.; 1 to 100 items |
| `files` | array of object | yes | One delivered file per item, in item order: the absolute path of the committed session artifact (decision D2). It is valid while the session exists (until it is closed, expires or is cleaned) and must not be written to; retain the session to keep the evidence.; 1 to 100 items |
| `files[].evidence_id` | string | yes | pattern `^evd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `files[].media_type` | "image/png" \| "audio/wav" | yes |  |
| `files[].path` | string | yes | 1 to 4096 characters |
| `partial_reason` | "frame_budget" \| "pixel_budget" \| "byte_budget" \| "session_evidence_budget" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "cancelled" or null | yes | Why the call returned fewer items than its request named, or null for a complete result. The items returned are committed evidence. Only complete records are reused. |

This schema also holds 4 conditional rules (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/frame-data.schema.json) for them.

### frame-evidence.schema.json

**VSift frame evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/frame-evidence.schema.json))

One published frame_evidence record (P09, ADR 0019): a whole displayed frame of the session's video, or a rectangle of one, extracted by frame get, frame neighbours, frame burst or crop. Its evidence_id digests only what fixes its pixels (session, source, stream, adapter profile, provider fingerprint, the frame's exact timestamp and time base, and a crop's region), so every request that resolves to the same frame names the same record; request-specific facts (requested time, policy, delta, candidate) are in the result's request and selections. The pixels are the delivered file named in the result's files, never embedded. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock_time` | any or any | no | The frame's real-world clock time, at (time anchoring, 0.3.0); absent when the session has no time anchor. See time-anchor.schema.json. |
| `clock_time.source` | "operator" \| "quicktime_creationdate" \| "container_creation_time" | yes |  |
| `clock_time.confidence` | "exact" \| "high" \| "medium" | yes |  |
| `clock_time.at` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.at.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.at.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.at.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |

### handoff-check-data.schema.json

**VSift handoff.check data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/handoff-check-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete handoff.check result (P13 PR 5, issue #213, ADR 0023 decisions G and H): whether an agent's draft report passed the skill's handoff checks. The command reads the whole report (at most 128 KiB of UTF-8 from standard input or --file; 64 KiB before 0.2.2), finds its one vsift-handoff block, reads closed values written in another letter case as the schema's spelling (case_notes), validates the JSON against the skill-owned handoff.schema.json and the handoff rules, and checks the whole report's text for local paths, links and raw hidden or control characters. With --session it also resolves every cited identity against that session's committed records, read-only; a closed, expired or unknown session is a gap in session, not a failure. valid is true exactly when errors is empty; the command exits 0 whenever it read the draft. No finding repeats text from the draft: pointer is an RFC 6901 pointer built from the handoff schema's own member names and array indices (an unknown member is reported at its object, with the allowed members), line is a 1-based line of the report, rule is closed, allowed lists the schema's own values where the rule has them, and message is fixed prose. Each list holds at most 100 findings; truncated says more were found.

### ingest-data.schema.json

**VSift ingest data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/ingest-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete ingest result. transcript is present only when a supplied transcript was imported with the session; a plain ingest omits it. time_anchor is present only when the session has a clock-time anchor. publication is the session's own guarantee: process_crash_consistent, or os_crash_durable for a durable session on the qualified profile (P10 engine API; P11 durable workspaces). Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json.

| `source_bytes` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `generation` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `publication` | "process_crash_consistent" \| "os_crash_durable" | yes |  |
| `expires_at` | string | yes | format date-time |
| `transcript` | object, see [transcript-revision.schema.json](#transcript-revisionschemajson) | no |  |
| `time_anchor` | object, see [time-anchor.schema.json](#time-anchorschemajson) | no | When the recording happened by the real-world clock, and on what authority (time anchoring, 0.3.0): from ingest --recorded-at, else the container's recording-time tags, which a plain ingest reads with one FFprobe run when the media tools are set up and verified. Absent when no clock time is known. |

### job-batch-data.schema.json

**VSift job.batch data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-batch-data.schema.json))

The data member of the terminal job.batch result (P11, ADR 0021): per-status counts, one item per line processed (at most 1,000; blank lines have none), the first line not started (after a shutdown, a line limit or an input error; null when every line was read) and why the batch stopped. Every request's full result was streamed before it as a result event (result-event.schema.json). The batch's exit status follows maintainer decision D5: 0 when every item is complete or partial, 6 when a shutdown stopped the batch, else the most severe failure class in the order 7 > 1 > 5 > 3 > 2 > 4.

| `items[].rejection` | "request_too_large" \| "request_too_deep" \| "malformed_request" \| "unsupported_schema_version" \| "invalid_operation_id" \| "invalid_session_id" \| "invalid_path" \| "invalid_transcript_offset" \| "invalid_deadline" \| "invalid_range" \| "invalid_bundle_name" \| "too_many_steps" \| "step_order" \| "no_work" \| "path_outside_input_root" \| "duplicate_operation_id" \| "workspace_not_durable" or null | yes |  |

### job-data.schema.json

**VSift job data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete job.status or job.cancel result: one recoverable job (P10, ADR 0020). Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json. state is what a reader observes: a job whose process ended without recording it is reported interrupted (or succeeded, when its commit is in the session's manifest chain), never running. live_owner says a process holds the job right now. resumable says whether job resume would run it now, and resumable_reason why (interrupted, not_started) or why not (live_owner, succeeded, failed, cancelled, session_not_open). operation_id is the id a retry should carry: the first one a caller bound with --operation-id, or for a succeeded job the one its commit is recorded under. request.range is the range the caller asked for (null for the whole source). progress.chunks_total is how many chunks the recognised range is cut into (null for a job created before P10 PR 3) and chunks_checkpointed how many chunk checkpoints the job keeps now (a succeeded, failed or cancelled job keeps none). attempts counts attempts in the job's current epoch. result names the revision and generation a succeeded job committed; failure the public code that ended the last attempt of an interrupted or failed job. A job never names a path, transcript text or provider output. Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033) a job of kind prepare, started by job.start, prepares a session: request.mode says how it runs (quick in the foreground, watched in the background by a runner, queued in the root's queue: first in, first out, one at a time a root, at the whole capacity, yielding it at every chunk boundary to anyone who waits for it, and publishing at its seal) and request.first the window it transcribes first, when one was named (--first), its progress counts are null and zero, and streams lists its started streams in the order they run (first: the window named with --first, retranscribed as a range on the whole run's chunk grid; visual: the visual-candidate index of the source, in batches of windows, with no job of its own; transcript: a whole-source retranscription): state is the stream's job's (not_started before it has one; for visual, running while the runner works on it, succeeded once every window is indexed, and skipped for a source without video), stage, chunks_done and chunks_total as the stream last reported them, published_until_us how far its revision is published (an open revision of the stream's job, or the whole range once it succeeded), and media how far it has come in media time ($defs.media_progress). streams appears for a prepare job only, and queue_position (0 for the next to run) for a queued prepare job that has not started.

### job-request.schema.json

**VSift worker job request v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-request.schema.json))

One request of `job run --request <file>`, or one line of `job batch --requests <file>` (P11, ADR 0021). Strict: every member is required except deadline_ms, unknown members are refused, and a document is at most 64 KiB and 16 levels deep. Paths are relative to the operator's --input-root with / between names; besides this pattern the decoder also refuses . and .. names, names ending in a dot or space and Windows device names (CON, NUL, COM1, ...). Steps run in order after the target: retain at most once and followed only by close; close at most once and last; a session target needs at least one step. The request digest is SHA-256 over 'vsift.job-request.v1', a line feed and the canonical serialization of the decoded request without its operation_id.

### job-result.schema.json

**VSift worker job result v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-result.schema.json))

The answer to one job request (P11, ADR 0021): the data of a job.run result and the result member of a job.batch result event. At most 64 KiB; it never names a path and never carries evidence text. status is derived: cancelled when the request or a step was cancelled, failed when it or a step failed, partial when a step left a stated gap, else complete. replayed is true when the recorded result of an earlier call with the same operation_id and request_digest was returned without new work. steps lists the ingest of an ingest target, then every requested step; after a failed or cancelled step the rest are not_started. A step's coverage: a candidates step always states it; a retranscribe step states it only when its run left part of its range untranscribed (the recogniser's answer for it could not be used; truncated, reason untranscribed_range, as transcript.retranscribe states it in its envelope; since 0.2.2), and is then partial; other steps have none. failure is the request's own failure (step null; rejection set when it was refused) or the failure of the step that ended it (step is that step's index).

The data member of a complete (or, since 0.2.1, partial) job.resume result (P10 PR 3): job is the job after the run (job-data.schema.json, normally succeeded), and outcome the retranscription it committed, exactly as transcript.retranscribe reports it (transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json; outcome.job.resumed says whether checkpoints were continued, outcome.job.replayed that the revision is an earlier commit returned again). ### job-start-data.schema.json

**VSift job.start data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/job-start-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete (or partial) job.start result (0.3.0, ADR 0033): job is the session's prepare job (job-data.schema.json) as it stands, start what the call did, and outcome, for a job that ran in the foreground, the retranscription it committed, exactly as transcript.retranscribe reports it (null otherwise). start.state is created (a new job), waiting (the same request's job, interrupted or not started, taken up again), restarted (a failed or cancelled one, started again from nothing), running (a runner holds it already; nothing was started) or done (it had succeeded; nothing was started). start.mode is quick (in the foreground: the call answers when the job is done, its revision sealed in one generation), watched (in the background: a runner publishes the revision as it goes and leaves one unit of the root's admission capacity free) or queued (in the background, after the root's earlier queued jobs, at the whole capacity, yielding it at every chunk boundary, publishing at the seal; only when asked for), and mode_basis why: requested with --mode, short_recording (under ten minutes), long_recording, or length_unknown (no transcript yet, so watched). start.runner is foreground, background (a runner was started and holds the job; detachment says how far it is detached from its caller: process_group on Unix, left_callers_job on Windows, or in_callers_job when the caller's job object forbids leaving it, so that whatever ends that job ends the runner) or none. Follow a background job with job.status; job.cancel or session.close stops it, and what it published stays. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job` | object, see [job-data.schema.json](#job-dataschemajson) | yes |  |
| `start` | object | yes |  |
| `start.state` | "created" \| "waiting" \| "restarted" \| "running" \| "done" | yes |  |
| `start.mode` | "quick" \| "watched" \| "queued" | yes |  |
| `start.mode_basis` | "requested" \| "short_recording" \| "long_recording" \| "length_unknown" | yes |  |
| `start.runner` | "foreground" \| "background" \| "none" | yes |  |
| `start.detachment` | "process_group" \| "left_callers_job" \| "in_callers_job" or null | yes |  |
| `outcome` | object, see [transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json](#transcript-retranscribe-dataschemajson) or null | yes |  |

### lifecycle-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL lifecycle event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/lifecycle-event.schema.json))

A worker host's own state in a job.run or job.batch --events jsonl stream (P11, ADR 0021; O-03): started (with its readiness: the sessions' publication guarantee, isolation, admission capacity and request concurrency), request_admitted, admission_waiting (reason admission_capacity, or since 0.3.0 queued_work: queued work holds the capacity and gives it back at its next chunk boundary, waited for up to 120 s; transcript.retranscribe, job.resume and job.start write this kind too, with line and request_operation_id null), request_finished (the request's status, failure code, rejection and dropped progress), draining (reason shutdown or drain_timeout) and stopped (reason end_of_input, shutdown, line_limit or input_error). ### ocr-search-data.schema.json

**VSift ocr.search data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/ocr-search-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial ocr.search result (0.3.0, ADR 0030 decision 13): one bounded page of the query's occurrences in the session's screen-text index, with or without a transcript. Occurrences are matched as search matches transcript segments (phrase, then all_terms) and ranked by tier, then by first appearance; a line read on consecutive read frames with the same words in the same place is one occurrence. Each hit cites its first frame, its region, its text and display_text, the runner's uncalibrated confidence, how long it stayed and the candidates of its frame (screen-text-data.schema.json#/$defs/hit). total_hits counts the whole search on every page. state is not_run before ocr has read the session, partial while its coverage of the searched range is not complete and complete otherwise; coverage is the screen-text coverage block. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial with a fixed warning, exactly when state is not complete; its reasons name not_run, or frames_pending, frames_failed, frames_awaiting_analysis and candidates_incomplete. Pass next_cursor back with the same session, query and range; it is rejected for any other search or session, after the session expires, or once ocr has committed a new index revision. Absence of a hit is never evidence the text was not on screen: only planned frames are read.

### progress-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL progress event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/progress-event.schema.json))

How far a long operation has come, in an --events jsonl stream (P11, ADR 0021): transcript.retranscribe and job.resume (chunks recognised, reused chunks included) the worker commands job.run and job.batch, and setup.install (fetching_artifact: bytes of the artifact being downloaded or imported; installing_components: components of the accepted plan finished). Advisory: at most one per second and 4,096 per request; an update inside the second replaces the pending one, and a host drops progress rather than block on a slow reader, counting the drops in progress_dropped (for this request, before this event). The terminal event stays authoritative. operation_id is null (the command's operation id is in the terminal event); request_operation_id names the worker request, null for other commands; job_id names the recoverable job, when the work runs as one. Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033) a recognising_speech event also carries media, how far the recognition has come in media time, with its speed and estimate ($defs.media_progress, the same definition as job-data.schema.json's, held equal by a contract test); job.start reports progress too. Every line is at most 64 KiB.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant "1" | yes |  |
| `event` | constant "progress" | yes |  |
| `sequence` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `command` | string | yes | at most 64 characters; pattern `^[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*(?:[.][a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*)?$` |
| `operation_id` | null | yes |  |
| `request_operation_id` | string or null | yes | at most 67 characters; pattern `^op_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `job_id` | string or null | yes | at most 68 characters; pattern `^job_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `stage` | "copying_source" \| "recognising_speech" \| "analysing_video" \| "running_request" \| "fetching_artifact" \| "installing_components" | yes |  |
| `completed` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `total` | integer or null | yes | at least 0 |
| `unit` | "bytes" \| "chunks" \| "windows" \| "steps" \| "components" | yes |  |
| `progress_dropped` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `media` | object | no | How far a recognition has come in media time (ADR 0033): done_us of total_us microseconds of the recording (total_us null when the end is not known), elapsed_ms of wall time in this attempt, speed in media seconds a wall second over the chunks recognised in this attempt (null before the first; chunks reused from checkpoints do not count), percent done rounded down (null without an end), and estimate, the wall time left as the media still to do over that speed (basis cumulative_measured_speed), null until at least two fresh chunks and 20 s of work have run, and in job.status only while a process runs the stream. Advisory: optimistic over silence. |
| `media.done_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `media.total_us` | integer or null | yes | at least 0 |
| `media.elapsed_ms` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `media.speed` | number or null | yes | at least 0 |
| `media.percent` | integer or null | yes | 0 to 100 |
| `media.estimate` | object or null | yes |  |
| `media.estimate.remaining_ms` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `media.estimate.basis` | constant "cumulative_measured_speed" | yes |  |
| `media.estimate.fresh_chunks` | integer | yes | at least 2 |

This schema also holds 6 conditional rules (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/progress-event.schema.json) for them.

### result-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL result event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/result-event.schema.json))

One worker request's complete result in a job.batch --events jsonl stream (P11, ADR 0021), written as soon as the request ends: line is its 1-based line in the batch file (null in job.run), result is job-result.schema.json. A refused line has no result event; its request_finished lifecycle event carries the rejection. Never dropped; at most 64 KiB per line.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |

| `event` | constant "result" | yes |  |
| `sequence` | integer | yes | at least 0 |

| `operation_id` | null | yes |  |
| `line` | integer or null | yes | 1 to 1000 |
| `result` | object, see [job-result.schema.json](#job-resultschemajson) | yes |  |

### screen-text-data.schema.json

**VSift ocr data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/screen-text-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial ocr result (0.3.0, ADR 0030): what one bounded call read of the on-screen text of a session's video with the optional OCR runner, and how much of the range's plan the session's screen-text index has read. The plan of a range is the representative frame of every visual candidate in it and one frame every coverage.period_us; a call reads at most --max-frames of its pending frames, commits one new index revision, and stops. Run ocr again for the same range to continue: it reads only what is pending. The text itself is found with search, whose first page carries a screen_text member ($defs/search_part) with each hit's frame, time and region. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial with a warning, exactly when coverage.pending or coverage.failed is not 0 or coverage.candidates_complete is false; then its gaps are the candidate_gaps that candidates can still fill, as from-to microsecond ranges, and its reasons name frames_pending, frames_failed and each of those gaps' reasons, once each, in that order. On-screen text is derived, untrusted evidence: quote display_text, and check the frame itself (frame get at the hit's time) before relying on a value.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `range` | object | yes | The range read: the requested range, or the whole video, clipped to the video. |
| `range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `index` | object or null | yes | The session's newest screen-text index revision after the call; null while no frame of the session has been attempted. |
| `index.index_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sti_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `index.revision` | integer | yes | 1 to 4294967295 |
| `index.engine` | object | yes | The engine build that read an index: the OCR runner, the ONNX Runtime it loaded and its two models, by version and digest. A different build starts a new index, so text read by two builds is never mixed. |
| `index.engine.profile` | "ppocrv5-latin-v1" | yes | ppocrv5-latin-v1: PP-OCRv5 mobile detection with the Latin-script recognizer, read with the runner's fixed settings. |
| `index.engine.runner_version` | string | yes | 1 to 64 characters; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` |
| `index.engine.runner_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `index.engine.runtime_version` | string | yes | 1 to 64 characters; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$` |
| `index.engine.detector_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `index.engine.recognizer_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `index.frames` | integer | yes | Frames the index holds, read or unreadable.; 0 to 4096 |
| `index.lines` | integer | yes | Lines of text the index holds.; 0 to 200000 |
| `read_now` | integer | yes | Frames this call attempted: read, or found unreadable.; 0 to 200 |
| `stopped` | "frame_limit" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "cancelled" \| "engine_failed" \| "media_failed" \| "index_full" or null | yes | Why the call ended with frames still pending, or null when it was not stopped. frame_limit: it read --max-frames frames. deadline_exceeded: its time ran out. cancelled: it was cancelled. engine_failed: the OCR runner failed and what it had read before is kept. media_failed: the media tools could not extract a frame. index_full (0.3.0, RV-2 finding 5): the index had room for no more frames (4,096 frames, 200,000 lines counted as 256 a frame), so the call read only what fitted; later calls by the same engine build read nothing more of this session. engine_failed also covers a runner whose files changed during the call (its build no longer the one the index records). Every stop keeps what was read before it. |
| `coverage` | object | yes | How much of the range's plan the index has read. Every planned frame is counted once: planned = read + failed + unresolved + pending; awaiting_analysis counts reads not yet planned. read: its frame was read (it may hold no text). failed: the runner rejected the image or failed on it; it is not read again by the same build. unresolved: the target time resolved to no decodable frame. pending: not attempted yet. Text that appears and goes between two planned frames is not read. |
| `coverage.scope` | constant "screen_text" | yes | What the block covers: on-screen text only. |
| `coverage.period_us` | integer or null | yes | The period of the frames planned between candidates: the call's --period-us (default 10000000). In search, the period of the index's latest call; null before ocr has run.; 1000000 to 600000000 |
| `coverage.planned` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.read` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.failed` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.unresolved` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.pending` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `coverage.awaiting_analysis` | integer | yes | Periodic reads of the range left out of the plan, not counted in planned, because their visual window is not analysed yet: always 0 when the call analyses missing windows itself, as vsift ocr does; counted by the engine's analysed-windows-only calls (ADR 0033's background prepare job). Coverage is not complete while it is above 0, and the envelope reason is frames_awaiting_analysis.; at least 0 |
| `coverage.candidates_complete` | boolean | yes | True when no visual window of the range is still to be analysed or tried again (not_analyzed, deadline_exceeded), so the plan holds every candidate the range will have. |
| `candidate_gaps` | array of object | yes | The visual index's gaps in the range, as candidates reports them, in start order. coverage.candidates_complete is false exactly while one of them can still be filled by candidates (not_analyzed, deadline_exceeded); the other reasons are final (their periodic reads are planned as anywhere else). At most 100 are listed.; at most 100 items |
| `candidate_gaps[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `candidate_gaps[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `candidate_gaps[].reason` | "not_analyzed" \| "deadline_exceeded" \| "undecodable" \| "no_decoded_frame" \| "candidate_budget_exhausted" | yes | The visual index's gap reason, as candidates-data.schema.json describes it; run candidates over the range to fill a not_analyzed or deadline_exceeded gap. |

### search-brief-data.schema.json

**VSift search data, brief view v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/search-brief-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial search result asked for with --view brief (0.2.1): search-data.schema.json with each item reduced to transcript-segment-brief.schema.json and a view member that is always brief. The parallel hits (segment_id and how it matched), the normalised query, the requested range, the cursor and transcript_coverage are the full page's own, and the revision block holds once what the full view repeats on every item. ### search-data.schema.json

**VSift search data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/search-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial search result: one bounded page of the transcript segments that match a literal query, in rank order (phrase matches first, then all-terms matches, each by segment start). items are the matching segments as published transcript evidence records (transcript-segment.schema.json), exactly as transcript.get returns them; hits names each item's segment_id and how it matched, in the same order. query.terms is how the query was normalised. range is the requested range, or null when the whole transcript was searched. transcript_coverage says which parts of the searched range a transcript covers: a word said in an untranscribed range cannot be found. Since 0.3.0 a first page also carries screen_text: the query's occurrences in on-screen text that ocr has read, with its own coverage; on-screen text is never part of items, hits, the cursor or transcript_coverage. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial, exactly when untranscribed_ranges is not empty. Pass next_cursor back with the same session, query, range and revision to continue; it is rejected for any other search, session or revision, or after the session expires.

| `query.terms` | array of string | yes | The normalised query words, in query order: lowercase letters and digits, with a decimal point only between digits.; 1 to 16 items; each: 1 to 1024 characters |
| `range` | object or null | yes |  |
| `range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `items` | array of object, see [transcript-segment.schema.json](#transcript-segmentschemajson) | yes | at most 100 items |
| `hits` | array of object | yes | at most 100 items |
| `hits[].segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^tsg_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |

| `screen_text.coverage.unresolved` | integer | yes | at least 0 |

| `since.since_token` | string | yes | 1 to 512 characters |
| `since.revision_state` | "open" \| "sealed" \| "stopped" | yes |  |
| `since.more` | boolean | yes |  |

### search-stream-data.schema.json

**VSift search JSON Lines terminal data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/search-stream-data.schema.json))

The data member of the complete or partial terminal result that ends a search --events jsonl stream. It is the page of search-data.schema.json without its items: the matching segments were the preceding evidence events (record_type transcript_segment, the same records transcript.get streams), in rank order, and record_count says how many there were. hits names each streamed segment and how it matched, in stream order. Pass next_cursor back with the same session, query, range and revision to stream the next page; null means the search is exhausted.

### setup-check-response.schema.json

**VSift setup.check response v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-check-response.schema.json))

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | constant "1" | yes |  |
| `command` | constant "setup.check" | yes |  |
| `profile` | "desktop" \| "worker" | yes |  |
| `status` | "ready" \| "degraded" \| "blocked" | yes |  |
| `verification_scope` | constant "executable_probe_only" | no |  |
| `local_asr_model` | constant "not_checked" | no | Kept constant for v1 compatibility; the local_asr object reports the model and its verification. |
| `local_asr` | object | no | Local speech recognition (added in P07 increment 3c). model: the registered model's identity against the reviewed pins. verification: whether whisper.cpp, the model and FFmpeg/FFprobe transcribed the reviewed speech clip built into VSift, from a recorded pass or run by this check within its own 60 s budget. Every detail field is present; those that do not apply to the status are null. |
| `local_asr.model` | object or object | yes |  |
| `local_asr.model.status` | "not_selected" \| "unreadable" \| "unrecognised" \| "known_pinned" | yes |  |
| `local_asr.model.profile` | null \| "base" \| "base_q5_1" | yes |  |
| `local_asr.verification` | object or object or object | yes |  |
| `local_asr.verification.status` | "verified" \| "failed" \| "not_run" | yes |  |

### setup-install.schema.json

**VSift setup install data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-install.schema.json))

The data of a setup.install result (P13, ADR 0023): every component of the accepted plan, in plan order (ffmpeg_ffprobe, whisper_cli, whisper_model), with what the transaction did to it. A successful result carries it as data; a failed or cancelled one carries the same object as data beside its error, whose code is the first failed component's failure_code. Each component activates atomically on its own: activated and already_current components are installed and selected; a rerun of the same accepted plan continues from the first component not yet current. A failed component names the step that stopped it and a typed reason; blocked means not activated because another component did not install: an earlier component of its part stopped it, or, since 0.3.0 (ADR 0036 section 4), video did not install and speech, downloaded and verified beside it, could not be tested; its verified download is then kept for the next run. stage says what cleanup did with the component's private stage (retained only when its ownership or content could not be proved). Every string is a closed identifier or a reviewed version; no path, URL, server text or credential.

### setup-list.schema.json

**VSift setup list data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-list.schema.json))

The data of a setup.list result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023): every core managed component, always in the order ffmpeg_ffprobe, whisper_cli, whisper_model, then (since 0.3.0, #409) each optional component the store holds a version or a selection of, js_runtime_deno then yt_dlp, with its selection, its selected and previous versions and every published version with whether it verifies. Read-only: listing creates and changes nothing. managed_install says whether managed installation can install on this host (catalogue_accepted only on Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64); managed_folder is absent when this user has no managed folder, and every component then has no versions. selection is verified when commands use the selected version (it verifies and its manifest is the one the selection names), unverified when they do not (the version is missing, does not verify or is being removed), unreadable when the selection cannot be read, and none when nothing is selected. A version's state is verified, removal_interrupted (a removal stopped; setup remove finishes it) or unverified with a fault. stale_stages and retained_stages count stages abandoned by earlier installations that setup remove --stale-stages would remove or would keep for the user. Every string is a closed identifier, a managed version key or fixed prose; no path.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `components` | array of object | yes | 3 to 5 items |

### setup-plan.schema.json

**VSift reviewed setup plan v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-plan.schema.json))

A read-only setup plan. Its intent (profile, target, managed_install, catalogue, plan_digest, every action's reviewed artifact, each dependency's and the model's disposition and next step) is what plan_digest binds and what setup install compares with a saved plan. Its observed state (readiness, install_needed, each dependency's and the model's status, each action's state) is what commands would use now, managed versions included (P13 PR 4): it changes as setup install applies the plan and is not compared, so a rerun of the same accepted setup install continues. An action whose state is current is installed at the plan's version; install_needed is false when every action is current or there is none.

### setup-remove.schema.json

**VSift setup remove data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-remove.schema.json))

The data of a setup.remove result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023), successful or failed. target is version (setup remove <component> --version <version>: one unselected version), component (setup remove <component>: its selection first, then every version) or stale_stages (setup remove --stale-stages: stages abandoned by interrupted or failed installations, and half-written selection pointers). Each version handled is listed with its status: removed, already_absent, in_use (a running job holds it; it is kept and a later setup remove removes it), selected, unexpected_content (an invalid manifest, a link, a folder or an unknown name: kept for the user) or storage_failure. Only positively identified content inside the private managed folder is ever removed; nothing is followed through a link. When anything asked for remains, the result is a failure (BUSY for a version in use, STORAGE_IO for kept content) with this same object as data beside the error. No path.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | "version" \| "component" \| "stale_stages" | yes |  |
| `component` | "ffmpeg_ffprobe" \| "whisper_cli" \| "whisper_model" \| "js_runtime_deno" \| "yt_dlp" or null | yes |  |
| `deselected` | boolean | yes |  |
| `versions` | array of object | yes | at most 1024 items |
| `versions[].component` | "ffmpeg_ffprobe" \| "whisper_cli" \| "whisper_model" \| "js_runtime_deno" \| "yt_dlp" | yes |  |
| `versions[].version` | string | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `versions[].status` | "removed" \| "already_absent" \| "in_use" \| "selected" \| "unexpected_content" \| "storage_failure" | yes |  |
| `stages` | object or null | yes |  |
| `stages.removed` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `stages.retained` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `stages.retention_reasons` | array of "ownership_unproved" \| "unexpected_content" \| "storage_failure" | yes | at most 3 items; items are unique |
| `stages.interrupted_selections_removed` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `next_step` | string | yes | 1 to 512 characters |

### setup-repair.schema.json

**VSift setup repair data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-repair.schema.json))

The data of a complete setup.repair result (P13 PR 6; ADR 0007 and ADR 0023: repair is read-only, it diagnoses and emits a plan). Repair changes, creates, selects and downloads nothing, and a store that needs repair is still a complete result: status is nothing_installed (no managed folder), healthy or needs_repair. Each finding says what is wrong (kind, the component and version concerned, a count for stages, pointers and entries, the fault of an unverified version), fix names how, summary is fixed prose, and command is the existing vsift command that applies the fix (an executable and argument array of fixed words and managed keys, run without a shell), or null for fix manual: content VSift cannot prove its own, which the user deletes. The findings are in the order to apply them. A reinstall is always a new setup plan accepted with setup install. No path.

| `status` | "nothing_installed" \| "healthy" \| "needs_repair" | yes |  |
| `findings` | array of object | yes | at most 4096 items |
| `findings[].kind` | "selection_unreadable" \| "selected_version_unverified" \| "version_unverified" \| "removal_interrupted" \| "stale_stages" \| "stages_need_manual_removal" \| "interrupted_selection" \| "unexpected_entries" | yes |  |
| `findings[].component` | "ffmpeg_ffprobe" \| "whisper_cli" \| "whisper_model" \| "js_runtime_deno" \| "yt_dlp" or null | yes |  |
| `findings[].version` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `findings[].count` | integer or null | yes | at least 1 |
| `findings[].fault` | "missing_manifest" \| "invalid_manifest" \| "changed_content" \| "unexpected_entry" \| "unreadable" or null | yes |  |
| `findings[].fix` | "rollback" \| "rollback_to_version" \| "remove_version" \| "remove_component_and_reinstall" \| "remove_stale_stages" \| "manual" | yes |  |
| `findings[].summary` | string | yes | 1 to 1024 characters |
| `findings[].command` | object or null | yes |  |
| `findings[].command.executable` | constant "vsift" | yes |  |

### setup-rollback.schema.json

**VSift setup rollback data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup-rollback.schema.json))

The data of a complete setup.rollback result (P13 PR 6, ADR 0023). Without --version the component returns to the version its selection records as selected before; with --version it selects that installed version. Either way the version is selected only after it verifies (its manifest exists and every file matches it; a return to the recorded previous version also requires the manifest recorded), in one atomic rename, and the version it replaced becomes the new previous one, so a second rollback returns. status is rolled_back, or already_selected when the named version was already the verified selection and nothing changed. A refusal (nothing installed, no such or earlier version, a version that does not verify, another command holding the managed folder) is a failure result and changes nothing. No path.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `component` | "ffmpeg_ffprobe" \| "whisper_cli" \| "whisper_model" \| "js_runtime_deno" \| "yt_dlp" | yes |  |
| `status` | "rolled_back" \| "already_selected" | yes |  |
| `selected_version` | string | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `replaced_version` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$` |
| `next_step` | string | yes | 1 to 512 characters |

### setup.schema.json

**VSift setup data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/setup.schema.json))

The data of a setup result: one unattended run of the setup door, vsift setup --unattended --install <parts> --json (ADR 0036 section 6). Naming the parts accepts the plan built for them; every artifact stays pinned and verified. outcome is pass when every named core part works after the run, also when nothing needed installing (exit 0), and fail when the install ran and a named part does not work (the exit status setup install gives the same failure). parts holds video, speech, then each included extra, with whether it was named, where it stands now and the one thing to do about it. install is the setup.install data of the install the run made, exactly as setup install reports it, or null when nothing needed installing. A run that could not start (a part VSift cannot install here, checks that ran out of time, a busy install, an --accept-plan digest that does not match) is the ordinary failure envelope, never this object.

### terminal-event.schema.json

**VSift JSONL terminal event v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/terminal-event.schema.json))

The last line of every --events jsonl stream; exactly one per stream. Its sequence is the number of events before it (0 when it is the only line, as for a failure before any other event; since P11 a failure after progress events follows them). A job.batch stream ends with job-batch-data.schema.json data after its lifecycle, progress and result events. Validate result with operation-response.schema.json and result.data with the command's data schema; a transcript.get stream ends with transcript-get-stream-data.schema.json data, and a search stream with search-stream-data.schema.json data, after its evidence events (evidence-event.schema.json).

### time-anchor.schema.json

**VSift time anchor v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/time-anchor.schema.json))

Time anchoring (0.3.0, ADR 0029): the time_anchor member of ingest and session status data, which says when the recording happened by the real-world clock and on what authority. It is present only when the session has an anchor; a session without one omits it, and every timestamped item then omits clock_time. An anchor ties one position of the timeline (media_time_us) to one clock reading from one source. The sources, in the order clock times are taken from them: operator (ingest --recorded-at, confidence exact), quicktime_creationdate (the recording app's own local-time tag, high) and container_creation_time (the container's UTC creation time, medium: many tools write the time they encoded or remuxed the file, and some devices the end of the recording). A file's modification time is never a source, and an online provider's upload date is not a recording time. consistency says whether the anchors agree: single (one anchor, or no two that name an instant), consistent (every two that name an instant agree within two seconds) or conflicting (two disagree; clock times still come from the first source, and a reader should say they are disputed). Only anchors that name an instant are compared: a local time whose zone is unknown (a clock face, or a statement without an offset) is never compared with another reading. Later releases may add sources (for example clocks visible on screen, at other positions of the timeline) and consistency values; a reader treats an unknown value as a reason to check the anchors list.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `consistency` | "single" \| "consistent" \| "conflicting" | yes |  |
| `source` | "operator" \| "quicktime_creationdate" \| "container_creation_time" | yes | The anchor every clock time of the session comes from: the first of anchors. |
| `confidence` | "exact" \| "high" \| "medium" | yes |  |
| `recording_start` | object or object | yes | The clock time of the start of the timeline (media time 0) by the selected anchor. |
| `recording_start.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `recording_start.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `recording_start.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `anchors` | array of object | yes | Every anchor, in the order clock times are taken from them.; 1 to 16 items |
| `anchors[].source` | "operator" \| "quicktime_creationdate" \| "container_creation_time" | yes |  |
| `anchors[].confidence` | "exact" \| "high" \| "medium" | yes |  |
| `anchors[].media_time_us` | integer | yes | The timeline position, in microseconds, whose clock reading this is. 0 for every source of 0.3.0.; at least 0 |
| `anchors[].time` | object or object | yes | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `anchors[].time.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `anchors[].time.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `anchors[].time.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |

This schema also holds 1 conditional rule (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/time-anchor.schema.json) for it.

### transcript-get-brief-data.schema.json

**VSift transcript.get data, brief view v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-get-brief-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial transcript.get result asked for with --view brief (0.2.1): transcript-get-data.schema.json with each item reduced to transcript-segment-brief.schema.json and a view member that is always brief. Everything else is the full page's own: the revision block holds once what the full view repeats on every item (revision_id, source_id, source_segment_id, the recognizer's digests, model and decoding profiles), and transcript_coverage says which parts of the range a transcript covers, exactly as in the full view. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json: its coverage member is truncated, and its status partial, exactly when transcript_coverage.untranscribed_ranges is not empty. The view is refused with --events jsonl. Pass next_cursor back with the same session, range and revision to continue; the view is not part of what a cursor binds, so it continues in either view.

### transcript-get-data.schema.json

**VSift transcript.get data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-get-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete or partial transcript.get result: one bounded page of the segments that intersect [range.from_us, range.to_us), in start order. transcript_coverage (0.2.1) says which parts of the requested range a transcript covers, by the rule search uses: nothing read in an untranscribed range means nothing was transcribed there, not that nothing was said.
