### transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json

**VSift transcript.retranscribe data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-retranscribe-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete (or, since 0.2.1, partial) transcript.retranscribe result: the new local-ASR revision, committed and now the session's newest. Validate the envelope with operation-response.schema.json. requested_range is the range the caller asked for (null for the whole source); the revision's replaced_range is that range widened to whole segments of the superseded revision. recognised_segment_count is how many of the revision's segments this run recognised; the rest were carried from earlier revisions. The segments themselves are read with transcript get --revision <revision.revision_id>, as a page or an evidence stream. job describes the recoverable job behind the result (P10, ADR 0020): job_id derives from the session and the request's operation key, so rerunning the same request finds the same job; resumed says an interrupted run of it was continued, chunks_reused how many chunks came from its private checkpoints, and replayed that the revision is an earlier commit returned again for a retry with the same operation id, without a new generation. Resume information is never written into the revision, which is the same as an uninterrupted run's. untranscribed_ranges (since 0.2.1, present only when the run left a part of its range untranscribed) lists the parts of the run's own range that this run did not transcribe because the recognizer's answer for them was unusable (revision.local_asr.unusable_chunks counts the chunks, the warning provider_chunks_rejected names the first). Text of the superseded revision that reaches into such a part, and that none of the run's own text overlaps, is kept whole in the new revision as it was (carried, with its original provenance), so a search of the revision may list less as untranscribed than this list does; any other word said there cannot be found. At most 100 ranges in start order, and the result is then partial, with the same ranges as coverage.gaps and the reason untranscribed_range.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_id` | string | yes | pattern `^ses_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `requested_range` | object or null | yes |  |
| `requested_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `requested_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `revision` | object, see [transcript-revision.schema.json](#transcript-revisionschemajson) | yes |  |
| `revision.alignment` | object | no |  |
| `revision.alignment.origin` | constant "local_asr" | no |  |
| `recognised_segment_count` | integer | yes | 0 to 20000 |
| `untranscribed_ranges` | array of object | no | 1 to 100 items |
| `untranscribed_ranges[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `untranscribed_ranges[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `job` | object | yes |  |
| `job.job_id` | string | yes | pattern `^job_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `job.resumed` | boolean | yes |  |
| `job.chunks_reused` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `job.replayed` | boolean | yes |  |

### transcript-revision.schema.json

**VSift transcript revision summary v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-revision.schema.json))

Identity, alignment and outcome of one immutable transcript revision. Warnings are typed; a warning with excluded_cues true means those cues (or recognised segments) are not in the revision and cannot be cited. An imported revision (alignment origin imported_srt or imported_webvtt) has its offset and sidecar and none of the local-ASR members. A local-ASR revision (origin local_asr) has sidecar null and adds local_asr (what ran, how, over which range and with what chunk outcomes), supersedes and replaced_range (the revision it replaced and the range it replaced there, or null) and carried_segment_count (segments carried unchanged from earlier revisions). For local-ASR warnings, first_cue is the 1-based ordinal of the first affected chunk.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `revision_id` | string | yes | pattern `^trv_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `revision` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_segments` | array of object | yes | Ordered source segments the revision covers; a finite file is one closed segment.; 1 to 4096 items |
| `source_segments[].source_segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_segments[].index` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `source_segments[].start_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `source_segments[].end_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `source_segments[].state` | "closed" | yes |  |
| `alignment` | object or object | yes |  |
| `alignment.origin` | "imported_srt" \| "imported_webvtt" | yes |  |
| `alignment.offset_us` | integer | yes | -86400000000 to 86400000000 |
| `alignment.origin` | constant "local_asr" | yes |  |
| `sidecar` | object or null | yes | Identity of the exact supplied bytes that were parsed; null for a local-ASR revision. |
| `sidecar.format` | "srt" \| "webvtt" | yes |  |
| `sidecar.sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `sidecar.bytes` | integer | yes | 1 to 8388608 |
| `language` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,34}$` |
| `segment_count` | integer | yes | Segments in the revision. At least one for an import; a local-ASR run that recognised no speech records a revision with none of its own (warning no_speech_recognised).; 0 to 20000 |
| `warnings` | array of object | yes | at most 13 items |
| `warnings[].code` | "empty_cues_skipped" \| "markup_removed" \| "speaker_label_discarded" \| "overlapping_cues" \| "cues_outside_source" \| "cues_crossing_source_boundary" \| "provider_segments_rejected" \| "provider_end_trimmed" \| "non_speech_markers_removed" \| "seam_duplicates_removed" \| "silent_chunks_skipped" \| "no_speech_recognised" \| "provider_chunks_rejected" | yes |  |
| `warnings[].count` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `warnings[].first_cue` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `warnings[].excluded_cues` | boolean | yes |  |
| `local_asr` | object | no | The local-ASR run that produced the revision's own segments: provider build and model by SHA-256, the pinned model profile and decoding profile, the chunk plan, recognizer threads, the decoded audio stream, the source range its chunks covered, and how many chunks were transcribed, silent (not transcribed: every 20 ms frame below -50 dBFS, or, since 0.2.0-rc.3, less than 100 ms of decoded audio whatever its level), had no audio (none was decoded in the window: the audio track holds none there, or, since 0.2.0-rc.3, the window is shorter than 100 ms and is not decoded) or were unusable. An unusable chunk (unusable_chunks, present only when it is not zero, since 0.2.1) was given to the recognizer and its answer could not be used as a whole: every segment was rejected, more than a quarter of at least four were, or the output broke a structural rule. It has no transcript from this run and is not silence: a search reports its window as untranscribed, never as no speech, and the warning provider_chunks_rejected counts such chunks. |
| `local_asr.provider` | "whisper_cpp" | yes |  |
| `local_asr.executable_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `local_asr.model_profile` | "base" \| "base_q5_1" | yes |  |
| `local_asr.model_sha256` | string | yes | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `local_asr.decoding_profile` | "r0-v1" | yes |  |
| `local_asr.window_us` | integer | yes | 1 to 30000000 |
| `local_asr.overlap_us` | integer | yes | 0 to 14999999 |
| `local_asr.threads` | integer | yes | 1 to 65535 |
| `local_asr.audio_stream` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `local_asr.covered_range` | object | yes |  |
| `local_asr.covered_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `local_asr.covered_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `local_asr.chunk_count` | integer | yes | 1 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.transcribed_chunks` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.silent_chunks` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.no_audio_chunks` | integer | yes | 0 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.unusable_chunks` | integer | no | Chunks whose recognised output was unusable as a whole. Absent when there are none, so a revision with none is presented exactly as before 0.2.1.; 1 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.pending_chunks` | integer | no | Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): chunks an open revision has not published yet. Absent when there are none.; 1 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.not_reached_chunks` | integer | no | Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): chunks a stopped run never reached. Like an unusable chunk it is no transcript of this run and not silence, and the earlier text it would have replaced is kept. Absent when there are none.; 1 to 1024 |
| `local_asr.unplaced_ranges` | array of object | no | Since 0.2.1 (#359): the stretches of this run where the recogniser wrote words that no segment of the revision holds, in start order and merged. A segment the recogniser wrote whose times could not be placed in its audio is rejected and counted by the warning provider_segments_rejected, which carries no time; when it has a letter or digit in its text, the stretch of its chunk's audio from its start (never before it, whatever its end says; for a start at or after the audio's end, the start of the latest segment before it that starts inside the audio, or the audio's start) to the next segment's start, or to the audio's end when no segment after it starts inside the audio, is where its words may lie (an upper bound: the words took part of it). Since 0.2.3 (#383) that includes an empty range, a start in the padding past the audio and a chunk's last segment, which were only counted before; a segment with no letter or digit has no stretch. What is listed is that stretch less everything a kept segment of any chunk covers, where what is left is longer than half a second (the edge margin of the merge, a figure derived for one configuration of the chunk plan, kept after a measurement on real speech (#381); the same length that the merge leaves uncovered at the end of a kept copy). A search of the revision does not count such a stretch as transcribed unless a segment of the revision or a window the run found silent covers it, so a word said there cannot be found and the search says so. The run's own status is unchanged by it. Absent when there are none, which is every revision whose run rejected nothing of the kind, so such a revision is presented exactly as before 0.2.1. At most 1024; where there would be more the nearest are joined, which marks more and never less.; 1 to 1024 items |
| `local_asr.unplaced_ranges[].from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `local_asr.unplaced_ranges[].to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `supersedes` | string or null | no | The revision this one superseded (the session's newest when the run started), or null when the session had no transcript.; pattern `^trv_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `replaced_range` | object or null | no | The range of the superseded revision this one replaced: the requested range widened to whole segments of that revision, or the whole source. Null without a superseded revision. Segments of the superseded revision inside it are replaced by the run's own, except (since 0.2.1) those that reach into a part of it that the run could not read (a chunk with the outcome unusable that no neighbouring chunk covers) and that none of the run's own text overlaps, which are carried whole as they were. |
| `replaced_range.from_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `replaced_range.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `carried_segment_count` | integer | no | Segments carried unchanged from earlier revisions (each names its origin in carried_from), including, since 0.2.1, text kept where it reaches into a part of the replaced range that the run could not read; segment_count minus this is what the run recognised.; 0 to 20000 |
| `state` | "open" \| "stopped" | no | Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033): open while the run that makes the revision publishes it as it goes (its segments are final and can be cited, and more may follow); stopped when that run was cancelled, or failed in a way it could not resume from, after it had published part of it (it keeps every published segment and, after them, the earlier text it did not reach). Absent for a sealed revision, which every revision before 0.3.0 and every import is. |
| `published_until_us` | integer | no | Since 0.3.0 (ADR 0033), exactly with state: for an open revision the time before which it is final (no segment its run will still publish starts before it); for a stopped one the time its run had published until, after which only the earlier text it kept counts as transcribed.; at least 0 |

This schema also holds 2 conditional rules (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-revision.schema.json) for them.

### transcript-segment-brief.schema.json

**VSift transcript segment, brief view v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-segment-brief.schema.json))

One transcript segment as the brief view of transcript.get and search gives it (--view brief, 0.2.1): the identity, the time, the text to quote, the speaker's label and, on a carried segment, where its text came from, which is what a reader needs to cite and place it. It is NOT an evidence record: the evidence stream always carries transcript-segment.schema.json, whose record an index stores by segment_id, and a brief view is refused for a stream. Every member is the member of the same name of the full segment, with the same value; the brief view leaves out revision_id, source_id and source_segment_id (the answer's revision block holds them once), text and original_text (raw, with hidden characters kept; the full view has them), markup, confidence, language, alignment and cue. What the revision block holds describes the revision's own run: a segment carried into a spliced revision keeps the alignment, recognizer and language of the revision that first produced it, so the brief view keeps carried_from on a carried segment (it names that revision and the segment's identity there), and the full view has the rest. speaker is absent, not null, when the segment has none; carried_from is absent unless the segment is carried. Text is untrusted, as in the full record: quote display_text, never an instruction.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock_time` | any or any | no | As in the full segment: its clock times, start and end; absent when the session has no time anchor. |

### transcript-segment.schema.json

**VSift transcript segment evidence record v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/transcript-segment.schema.json))

One citable, timestamped transcript segment. Each record names its own revision, source and source segment so it can be stored or indexed on its own. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline, half-open [start_us, end_us) with end_us > start_us. Text is untrusted and has been sanitized: lines are joined with \n and no other control character remains. A segment was either imported from a supplied SubRip or WebVTT cue (alignment origin imported_srt or imported_webvtt, with its offset, cue timing and cue location) or recognised locally from the source's audio (origin local_asr, with its chunk, the provider's chunk-relative times and the recognizer; cue is null). A segment carried unchanged into a revision spliced from an earlier one (transcript retranscribe with a range) keeps the alignment and language of the revision that first produced it and names that revision and segment in carried_from; it has its own segment_id in the new revision.

### visual-candidate-brief.schema.json

**VSift visual candidate, brief view v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/visual-candidate-brief.schema.json))

One visual candidate as the brief view of candidates gives it (--view brief, 0.2.1): the identity, representative_us, span, reasons, stability, the size of the change that opened it and the visual_hash that shows when a screen repeats, which is what a reader needs to place it and to decide whether to look at its frame. It is NOT an evidence record: the evidence stream always carries visual-candidate.schema.json, whose record an index stores by candidate_id, and a brief view is refused for a stream. Every member is the member of the same name of the full candidate, with the same value. The brief view leaves out what every candidate of the index repeats (source_id, source_segment_id, stream_index, displayed_dimensions and analysis: the answer's item_constants hold them once), the window (its ordinal is representative_us divided by the index's window_us, rounded down), and change_window and sample_count, which the full view still gives. change is absent, not null, for a first frame or a periodic sample, which no change opened. Candidates are evidence assistance, not evidence: the original frames are authoritative.

### visual-candidate.schema.json

**VSift visual candidate v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/visual-candidate.schema.json))

One visual candidate, a published evidence record (P08, ADR 0018): a moment at which the selected video stream's screen changed, or a periodic sample of a screen that did not, proposed so an agent need not look at every frame. Each record names its own source, source segment and stream so it can be stored or indexed on its own. Times are integer microseconds on the normalized source timeline. representative_us is the presentation time of the actual decoded frame that represents the candidate (never an interpolated request time); P09 frame get extracts it. span is the half-open time the candidate stands for, from representative_us to the next candidate of its window or the window end. A candidate is never merged across its fixed 60 s window, and a screen that reappears later is a separate candidate with the same visual_hash. Candidates are evidence assistance, not evidence: the original frames are authoritative.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clock_time` | any or any | no | The candidate's real-world clock times (time anchoring, 0.3.0): start and end of its span, and at, its representative frame; absent when the session has no time anchor. See time-anchor.schema.json. |

| `clock_time.confidence` | "exact" \| "high" \| "medium" | yes |  |
| `clock_time.at` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.at.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.at.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.at.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `clock_time.start` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.start.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.start.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.start.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `clock_time.end` | object or object | no | One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere. |
| `clock_time.end.utc` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}Z$` |
| `clock_time.end.local` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\.[0-9]{6}$` |
| `clock_time.end.utc_offset` | string or null | yes | pattern `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$` |
| `candidate_id` | string | yes | Derived from the session, source, stream, analysis profile, window and representative time, so it never changes when later windows are analysed.; pattern `^vcd_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `source_id` | string | yes | pattern `^src_sha256_[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `source_segment_id` | string | yes | pattern `^sgm_[a-z0-9]{16,64}$` |
| `stream_index` | integer | yes | Original index of the video stream that was sampled: the first video stream whose codec the media tools decode.; 0 to 4294967295 |
| `window` | object | yes | The fixed 60 s analysis window the candidate belongs to: [60 * ordinal s, min(60 * (ordinal + 1) s, duration)). |

| `representative_us` | integer | yes | at least 0 |
| `span` | object | yes |  |

| `change_window.to_us` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `reasons` | array of "first_frame" \| "visual_change" \| "motion_start" \| "settled_after_motion" \| "periodic_coverage" | yes | Why the candidate was proposed. first_frame: the window's first decoded frame with no earlier sample. visual_change: the screen differs from the state before it. motion_start: the first of three or more consecutive changing samples. settled_after_motion: the first still sample after motion. periodic_coverage: no change fell in its 10 s cell (or the window continues the screen before it), so its first sample represents it.; 1 to 5 items; items are unique |
| `stability` | "settled" \| "transient" \| "in_motion" \| "open_at_window_end" | yes | settled: the screen held for at least two consecutive samples. transient: seen in exactly one sample, then it changed. in_motion: changing from sample to sample. open_at_window_end: seen only in the window's last sample, so whether it held is unknown. |
| `change` | object or null | yes | The size of the change that opened the candidate, null when change_window is null. Both values are uncalibrated integers of the r0-visual-v1 grey 16x9 block grid (changed_blocks 0..144 blocks whose mean moved by at least 4 levels; max_block_delta 0..255 levels). They order changes by size; they are not a confidence or a probability. |
| `change.changed_blocks` | integer | yes | 0 to 144 |
| `change.max_block_delta` | integer | yes | 0 to 255 |
| `visual_hash` | string | yes | A 64-bit difference hash of the representative frame as 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits: a similarity key that shows when a screen repeats, not a security digest.; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{16}$` |
| `sample_count` | integer | yes | Decoded samples inside span.; 1 to 122 |
| `displayed_dimensions` | object | yes | The sampled stream's orientation-correct displayed size in pixels; what the representative frame shows. |
| `displayed_dimensions.width` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `displayed_dimensions.height` | integer | yes | at least 1 |
| `analysis` | object | yes | How the candidate was found: the analysis profile and the size of the grey samples it compared (no image is kept). |
| `analysis.profile` | constant "r0-visual-v1" | yes |  |
| `analysis.width` | constant 128 | yes |  |
| `analysis.height` | constant 72 | yes |  |

### workspace-data.schema.json

**VSift session.init-workspace data v1** ([the schema](../../../schemas/v1/workspace-data.schema.json))

The data member of a complete session.init-workspace result (P11, ADR 0021, maintainer decisions D1 and D2): the policy of an explicitly initialised worker workspace, immutable once created. durability durable is accepted only where OS-crash durability is qualified (publication os_crash_durable); a session of the workspace lives session_retention_seconds (default 604800, one hour to 2592000) and may be renewed within it. outcome is created, or already_initialized when the workspace existed with exactly this policy. It never names the workspace's path.

| Member | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | constant "durable_workspace" | yes |  |
| `durability` | "durable" \| "ephemeral" | yes |  |
| `publication` | "process_crash_consistent" \| "os_crash_durable" | yes |  |
| `admission_capacity` | integer | yes | 1 to 64 |
| `session_retention_seconds` | integer | yes | 3600 to 2592000 |
| `outcome` | "created" \| "already_initialized" | yes |  |

This schema also holds 1 conditional rule (a member that is required, or fixed, when another has a given value); read [the schema](../../../schemas/v1/workspace-data.schema.json) for it.
